lines.en: label toukaarchery20:
scene toukatsuneyoarchery1
I, once again, take it upon myself to intrude on Wakana’s domain in an effort to get closer to a girl who may one day own this entire city.
She is joined, of course, by a girl who will likely never own anything apart from the most popular ramen shop in the entire old district (Out of what I can only assume is one.)
And while they are certainly an odd pairing, they’re not without their similarities as well.
They both grew up sheltered. Neither one of them is good at socializing. And they could probably kill me within a matter of minutes if they wanted to.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery2
: Ha!
Or seconds in Tsuneyo’s case. Touka’s team of assassins (That I definitely know she has) would probably take a little longer to properly coordinate.
: Almost there, Tsuneyo! Though, I can’t help but wonder if your shots would be any more accurate if you’d put less power behind them.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery3
: Weapons were made for inflicting harm. Normally upon other people with weapons.
: But in this case, my enemy is a circle. And so I will attack with every last bit of power I have.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery4
: I am Tsuneyo Tojo, slayer of shapes!
: Ha!
scene toukatsuneyoarchery5
: Oh my. That one managed to pierce straight through the wall.
: The wall is my enemy as well.
: Please don’t go destroying school property in front of me. I think I’m supposed to report it or something.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery6
: Oh, Sensei. Good morning. I was unaware you’d be joining us today.
: But I suppose I should have expected it on account of your newfound affinity for stalking me at my morning practices.
: What?
: I apologize. Did you not recently come here to watch me, only to subsequently spend the day with my mother and then proceed to forget about me entirely?
: I did. But why do you sound so bitter about this?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery7
: The heart of a woman is a complicated thing. But the heart of a warrior is easy to understand. Shoot. Kill. Repeat.
: Take aim at the shape before you...then steel your resolve and turn it into a tree.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery8
: Ha!
: It hit the wall again, didn’t it?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery9
: Perhaps it is time for me to review the basics once more.
: Excellent idea, Tsuneyo. Why don’t you go have Miss Watabe teach you once more so I can spend the morning reminding our dear teacher to stop getting involved in my mother’s affairs?
: Yes, Master.
: And please stop calling me “Master.” Even if I do enjoy the sound of it.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery10
Tsuneyo scans her surroundings to make sure the coast is clear before collecting her arrows (Or at least the few that didn't break) at the opposite end of the archery range.
Back on this side, however, it appears that I am in trouble?
: Well? Do you have anything to say to me?
: You...look very pretty today?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery11
: Something I am not already aware of?
: Are you...looking for an apology or something? What’s going on here?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery12
: That’s what I would like to know. Why are you suddenly so...gung-ho in terms of watching my morning practices? You hardly seem like the type to enjoy this sport.
: Are you only saying that because I'm a commoner?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery13
: Yes.

: But also because, at least from my perspective, it appears that your key interests are limited to flirting with the girls in class. And surely you wouldn’t flirt with me while there are sharp objects around.
On second thought, maybe Touka’s team of assassins is closer than I previously believed.
: It would be one thing if you were to take an interest in kyudo, but any woman in my position would be reasonably put off by someone coming to just watch for no reason at all.
: It seems unfair that your mom is allowed to but I’m not.
: My mother carried me inside of her body for nine months and then proceeded to nurture me afterward. Comparing yourself to her is just silly.
: Fine. I guess I’ll just have to carry you around for nine months to make up for lost time. Come here, I’ll give you a ride back to the main building.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery14
: What do you want, Sensei? And why can’t it wait until I’m not in the middle of morning practice? Disrupting one’s schedule for your own personal gain is exceptionally rude.
: I’m glad you asked, Tsuneyo. Because there’s something I’ve been wanting to talk to you about and now is the best time for me.
: Sorry, are you talking to me? Because Tsuneyo is still collecting her arrows and my name is Touka. To-u-ka. Say it with me. To-
: Come on, Tsuneyo. Let’s talk in the shade.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery15
: ...Yes. Let’s do that.
scene black
I convince Tsuneyo 2 to follow me behind the archery building so the two of us can talk without worrying about any rogue arrows or the possibility of being spotted with one another.
Not because I think anyone would assume something, but because there actually is something I want to talk to Touka about and I don’t want to risk being interrupted.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery16
But before that, I should try and clear up whatever misunderstanding she very obviously has about her mother and me.
: Just so you know, I haven’t boned your mom.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery17
There. That should take care of it. Now I can move on to-
: Why would you open the conversation like that? That was perhaps the worst possible way to get me to pay any attention to whatever it is you want to discuss today — which is apparently my mother.
: It’s not. Well, it is. Kind of. But I only opened like that because you’re clearly upset about me hanging out with her here and that is unfair to me — a man who came to here to see you.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery18
: I believe you. But that doesn’t change the fact that she is now caught up and interested in both your personal affairs and mine.
: I thought you wanted her to be more interested in your “personal affairs” though? What with the two of you barely ever seeing each other and everything.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery19
: Yes, but not like this. The ordeal with the apartment complex was meant to be something I handle on my own to show her I’m capable of taking on additional responsibilities.

: Now, I’m being slowly pushed out of my own purchase all because she’s incapable of keeping her hands clean from anything that interests her. Which just so happens to be real estate and project management.
: No offense to you or your mom, but those are some pretty boring interests.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery20
: To you, I’m sure. But people love what they love. And my mother has a hard time letting things go once she becomes absorbed in them.
: I’m not sure how it happened this time, exactly-
: But seeing as you just so happen to be the only resident of my complex and have been spending time with my mother recently, you can’t blame me for assuming you have something to do with this.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery21
: I mean...I won’t say I don’t have anything to do with it. But I wish she’d stay out of this just as much as you do.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery22
: You do? Why? I was under the impression the two of you were working together to some extent. Did I misunderstand?
: Probably. In fact, the only reason she’s “working” with me at all is because I can do something she can’t.
: Well, yes. That’s the only reason partnerships exist in the first place. There’d be no reason to work together on something one could accomplish on their own.
: But, and I apologize for how offensive this may sound, I highly doubt there is anything you can do that my mother can not.
: It’s something that involves Chika.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery23
: Chika? How did she get wrapped up in all of this? I was unaware you were even telling anyone about the building.
: Has Tsubasa really not told you anything?
: Not really, no. She did mention something about a plan for leasing the remaining rooms out, but I’m not privy to the specifics.
: And seeing as the complex is technically owned by the Tsukioka Foundation and not specifically me, my hands are tied. She can do whatever she wants with this listing and I can’t stop her.
: I actually don’t even have to be informed. So, unless she goes out of her way to specifically advise me of her plans, I’ll remain in the dark altogether.
: Can I advise you of her plans? Or will you go and tell her that I came clean right away and destroy the rapport I have with her?
: Is there any particular reason you need to continue building a rapport with her?
: Yes. But I can’t tell you what it is until you’re older.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery24
: You’re a disgusting man. You do know this, right?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery25
: Yeah. Just wait until you hear the rest, though.
: Like I said, the reason Tsubasa is suddenly so interested in this building isn’t because of me at all. It’s because of Chika and her sister.
: Your mom is unhappy with the condition of the building they’re living in-
: And for good reason. That apartment is held together by duct tape and Elmer’s glue.
: But Chika doesn’t want to leave it since all of her childhood memories are there.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery26
: I see...

: So now, there’s this huge plan where I’m supposed to convince Chika to move into the building. But it came out of nowhere and I feel like I can’t even get out of it because Tsubasa’s too...commanding.
: May I ask why you want to get out of it?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery27
: There’s more than enough room in that building for Chika. And I’d allow them to stay free of charge as I’m aware of Chinami’s condition and know that tragedy could strike at any moment.
: The closer she is to adequate care, the safer she’ll-
: Chika...kind of thinks that we’re dating.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery28
: And...why does she think that, exactly?
: I see.
: If I ask her to come live in the same building as me, it’ll turn into a whole thing. Like, yeah, I could probably make it happen under the guise of it all being real, but-
: How long has she thought this, exactly?
: Long?
scene toukatsuneyoarchery29
: ...Yeah.
: And you never bothered clearing things up with her?
: No...and it’s kind of too late at this point, so...
: I’ve sort of just...accepted it.
: I suddenly understand your resistance.
: If Chika remains distant from you, it will be easier to continue shying away from the true nature of your relationship and what that means to you as opposed to what it means to her.
: And...just based on what I’ve seen and heard...would likely prevent her from questioning you in the event that others who may think the same thing she does wind up in that building as well.
: People like Maya. Or Makoto.
: Did Makoto tell you?
: Not directly. But it wasn’t hard to pick up on once the two of us started growing closer.
: Gotcha....that’s basically the situation, then. And I feel weird talking to you about it like this, but I really just don’t know what else I’m supposed to do.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery30
: Do you at least understand how I feel having to be the one to talk about this with you?
: Not really, no.
: Of course you don’t. Because it is more convenient for you to not understand that. Plus, you are an idiot.
: But instead of spelling it out for you, I’ll play my part and offer you a piece of advice instead.
: If that is okay with you, of course. I could just keep my mouth closed and let you sort this out with my mother. But good luck trying to get her to cease fire in any regard whatsoever.
: What do you think I should do?
: You’re not going to like it. I will warn you right now. Do you still want to hear it regardless?
: It’s not like I’ve got any other ideas. And, like you said, the chances of me getting Tsubasa to back down are slim to none.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery31
: I see.
: Then, I think you need to grow up.
: There are far greater problems in this world than whether or not you break the heart of a girl in the springtime of her youth.

: You’re an adult and you should act like one. Which means having a backbone and making your own decisions instead of waiting for everyone else to change and mold every given situation to fit your needs.
: The fact of the matter is, Chika and her sister will be safer in a new housing complex.

: Will that make your life harder and a bit less convenient? Yes. But I ask you to think of how much better it will make their lives since you apparently haven’t done that of your own volition just yet.
: I’m not sure I follow. Getting Chika to move in wouldn’t require breaking her heart. It would be the exact opposite. Asking her to come live there would make her extremely happy.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery32
: At first, yes.
: But how would she feel the moment she sees someone else leaving your room? That’s what you’re afraid of, isn’t it?
: No matter how secretive you be, she’ll always be right down the hall. And she could catch you at any moment.
: I haven’t even...done anything like that in the apartment, though.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery33
: Then gaining a few new neighbors wouldn’t disrupt your habits at all. It would just prevent new ones from forming. Which, in this context, sounds like it could be a good thing.
: I told you you wouldn’t like what I had to say. Every last bit of it makes your life worse and everyone else’s life better. That is essentially a narcissist’s Kryptonite.
: Did I say that correctly? Kryptonite? That’s the superhero gem, right?
: You know, you really do take after your mom.
: Because I’m beautiful and smart?
: Sure, there are those things. But it’s mostly because you’ve both found a way to put yourself on a pedestal miles above everyone else without seeming entirely pompous about it.
: Generosity goes a long way in bringing people over to one’s side. You should try it some time.
scene toukatsuneyoarchery34
: Sounds exhausting.
: Oh...you don’t know the half of it...
scene black
As I leave the archery range, I feel a little bad about emptying my problems out all over Touka.
But, for the sake of creating another fun new comparison that may or may not be symbolic in some sort of way, I will now do several things.
The first of which is having you imagine that my problems are a liquid.
The second is recalling what I said moments ago about how similar Touka and her mother are.
The third is forgetting that.
And the fourth is wrapping back around to my liquid problems and finalizing the comparison by telling you Tsubasa’s skin is hydrophobic.
Her daughter’s is not.
